authority: Top-level project overview and entry point
purpose: Introduces the project, states the specification-stage status, summarizes the planned design, and links the documentation set.
update_when: the documented interface or flags change

authority: Authoritative change history for all released and unreleased versions
purpose: Records notable additions, changes, and fixes in Keep a Changelog format.
update_when: a version is released or tagged
the project leaves the specification stage

authority: Primary end-user documentation for the CLI
purpose: Explains planned workflows, flags, statuses, version matching, TUI keys, safety, and troubleshooting.
update_when: a flag, status, matching rule, or TUI key changes
user-visible behavior is implemented or changed

authority: Maintainer and operator guidance for building, releasing, and operating the tool
purpose: Documents prerequisites, build and version injection, release process, security and privacy checklist, and recovery.
update_when: the build or release process changes
a security or privacy control changes

purpose: Lists durable design decisions, their status, and the requirement IDs they satisfy.
update_when: an ADR is added, superseded, or its status changes

authority: Design decision: ship as a single static Go binary with an embedded catalog
purpose: Records the decision to build one static binary with an embedded, versioned catalog and three target platforms.
update_when: the packaging or distribution model changes

authority: Design decision: report-only, never install or execute repository code
purpose: Records the report-only and credential-neutral security posture.
update_when: the trust or execution model changes

authority: Design decision: offline by default with opt-in additive enrichment
purpose: Records the offline-by-default guarantee and the additive, non-blocking enrichment contract.

authority: Design decision: declarative files are the authoritative source
purpose: Records the deterministic detector model and conservative README parsing.
update_when: the detector set or detection policy changes

authority: Design decision: loose, transparent version matching that warns
purpose: Records constraint interpretation and warn-not-fail status semantics.

authority: Design decision: swappable, shell-free, bounded probe backend
purpose: Records the probe backend interface, shell-free execution, and concurrency and timeout bounds.
update_when: the probing model or limits change

authority: Design decision: stable versioned JSON and a fixed exit-code contract
purpose: Records the JSON schema compatibility contract and the 0/1/2 exit-code semantics.
update_when: the JSON schema or exit codes change

authority: Design decision: keyboard-driven TUI with an accessible plain mode
purpose: Records accessibility requirements: no color-only status, keyboard completeness, and plain mode.
update_when: TUI interaction or accessibility behavior changes

authority: Design decision: bounded scanning and a safe remote-clone lifecycle
purpose: Records scan depth, denylist, gitignore, no-submodule, and temp-clone cleanup rules.
update_when: scan limits or clone lifecycle change

purpose: States which versions have been released and links their notes.
update_when: a release note file is added or renamed

authority: Planned v1 scope draft (not a release)
purpose: Captures the planned v1 scope, compatibility, limitations, and validation status before implementation.
update_when: the first release is implemented or tagged

title: repo-ready Documentation Map
instructions: Read the relevant source-of-truth documents before changing behavior, and update affected documents in the same change.
This map tracks the README and the documentation set created for the specification-stage documentation pass; the PRD and feature specifications are intentionally not mapped yet.
When several mapped documents may be affected, review critical and high priority entries first.
When a mapped document is added, removed, or renamed, update docmap.jsonl in the same change.
Keep paths repository-relative and do not add generated or vendored documents unless explicitly approved.
